subject: DPF evidence & integration / ops clarifications (Sunrise Health)
messages:
From: Sundar Rao <sundar.rao@sunrisehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sunrise Health Legal <privacy@sunrisehealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@sunrisehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: DPF evidence & integration / ops clarifications

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the initial DPF packet. Our security and integrations teams reviewed it and have a handful of operational clarifications before we move to the procurement stage. High level asks:

- Confirm which Redis/KV caches (hosted vs customer-managed) may hold personal data during inference and whether they are covered by the same technical measures in the DPF.
- Current subprocessor list shows third-party monitoring vendors; please confirm whether any of those vendors process logs that contain raw prompt text.
- Clarify cross-border fallback behavior: if a US region instance is saturated and requests failover to EU nodes, do we get an audit trail per-request showing origin and final processing region?
- We need a short ops checklist that our SREs can run during integration (network ACLs, egress IPs, TLS cert pinning guidance).

Target timeline: procurement team would like concrete answers + evidence by Friday, 18 June. If you can provide a single bundle with runbooks and logs examples (sanitized), that would be ideal.

Also: are on-prem (air-gapped) inference packages available for our pilot? If so, we need a list of the platform dependencies & minimum hardware spec.

Thanks,
Sundar
Director, Integrations
Sunrise Health

Attachments referenced: none (we received your packet via the Drive link).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sundar Rao <sundar.rao@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Sunrise Health Legal <privacy@sunrisehealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@sunrisehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPF evidence & integration / ops clarifications

Sundar —

Thanks — appreciate the clear asks. See answers inline below and attached evidence bundle (redwood-dpf-technical-evidence-20270614.zip). I also uploaded a copy to the secure Drive folder here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/DPF/SUN-4983/evidence

Inline:
- Redis/KV caches: our hosted runtime uses in-process KV caches and optionally a managed Redis for some high-throughput configurations. By default, the KV cache stores token-level state transiently and is encrypted at rest when using Redwood Dedicated/Private. The evidence bundle includes the KV encryption config, key lifecycle notes, and a sample purge policy we recommend.

- Monitoring vendors & logs: third-party monitoring (LogPulse) collects aggregate metrics only by default. Raw prompt text is never sent to monitoring unless a customer enables debug tracing; that requires an explicit opt-in and is logged as an event. See attachment: subprocessor-ops-table.csv (column "raw_prompt_access").

- Cross-border fallback & auditing: yes — our smart routing adds a per-request audit record (route decision, timestamp, final node region). The evidence set includes a sample audit record (sanitized) and the retention policy. When a fallback occurs we log origin IP block + final processing region; the logging pipeline is accounted for in the DPF.

- Ops checklist: added dataflow-integration-diagram.pdf and an "Integration SRE checklist" text file in the zip. It contains required IP CIDR ranges, TLS requirements, and suggested ACLs.

- On-prem package: yes, we offer a Private on-prem bundle for pilots (air-gapped option available). Minimum spec: 4x A10 GPUs, 512GB RAM, 8TB NVMe, and an orchestration node (Ubuntu 22.04). The package requires an HSM or KMS integration for key management; see section 3 of the attached runbook.

Next steps: we can sign a limited DPA Annex amendment and provide the on-prem installer under an evaluation agreement. Would you like me to route a DPA Annex redline to your legal contact for signature?

Attaching: redwood-dpf-technical-evidence-20270614.zip (contains dataflow-integration-diagram.pdf, subprocessor-ops-table.csv, integration-sre-checklist.txt)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Privacy Solutions, Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick internal notes before we finalize the bundle to Sunrise:

On caching: the majority of customers never opt into Redis-backed KV; we should call that out explicitly and provide the config flags to disable it. Can you add a short example of a startup flag for Dedicated that disables external Redis to avoid confusion? (Connor: can you paste the snippet from the runtime repo?)

On monitoring: redact the single sample log in the bundle further to remove all UUIDs and replace with placeholders — legal asked for maximal de-identification.

On on-prem: procurement will want a concise support matrix. I suggest a one-page table: feature / supported in Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Marissa, can you add that to the zip as "support-matrix.png"?

Finally: we should propose a 30-minute integration call for Wed, Jun 16 (US morning) to walk the SREs through the checklist. Marissa, if you agree I can propose slots.

-Karthik
VP, Product Engineering
